title: From brain networks to the patient-environment system in clinical neuroimaging
title_zh: 从脑网络到临床神经影像中的患者-环境系统
abstract: Despite substantial advances in clinical neuroimaging, its impact on defining and treating psychiatric disorders remains limited. Current approaches in clinical brain imaging frame psychiatric disorders as dysfunctions of brain-based information processing. Here, we propose a shift in this explanatory focus, from how aberrant neural processes generate maladaptive behavior to the brain's participation in the dynamics of the patient-environment system. Drawing on organism-environment approaches, we conceptualize behavior as emerging from context-dependent coordinated interactions among brain, body, and environment. Within this framework, we conceptualize psychiatric disorders as excessive stability or flexibility in patient-environment dynamics that impair the patient's capacity to adapt to changing situations. After examining the ontological commitments of current clinical neuroimaging and recasting psychiatric disorders in terms of patient-environment dynamics, we outline concrete strategies for operationalizing this framework. These progress from combining ecological momentary assessment with neuroimaging, to naturalistic brain and body imaging that jointly tracks neural, bodily, and environmental dynamics, and finally to explicit dynamical models of the patient-environment system in which maladaptive stability or flexibility can be formally defined and identified. By making these dynamics measurable, we aim to turn a conceptual reframing into a concrete empirical program, recasting the brain not as the seat of psychiatric disorders but as one participant in the patient-environment dynamics.
abstract_zh: 尽管临床神经影像取得了显著进展，但其在定义和治疗精神疾病方面的影响仍然有限。目前的临床脑成像方法将精神疾病视为基于脑的信息处理失调。在此，我们提出将解释焦点从异常神经过程如何产生不适应行为转向大脑在患者-环境系统动力学中的参与。借鉴机体-环境方法，我们将行为概念化为大脑、身体与环境在情境依赖下协调互动的产物。在此框架下，精神疾病被视为患者-环境动力学中过度的稳定性或灵活性，削弱了患者适应变化情境的能力。在审视当前临床神经影像的本体论承诺并将精神疾病重新表述为患者-环境动力学后，我们概述了将该框架操作化的具体策略。这些策略从将生态瞬时评估与神经影像相结合，到自然环境下的脑体成像共同追踪神经、身体与环境动态，最终到明确的患者-环境系统动力学模型，在其中可以正式定义和识别不适应的稳定性或灵活性。通过使这些动力学可测量，我们旨在将概念重构转化为具体的实证计划，将大脑重新定位为患者-环境动力学中的参与者，而非精神疾病的根源。
